cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) is not shutting the door on judgment here, because in Jerusalem he himself tells the crowd to *judge righteous judgment*. What he turns away in the Sermon is the crooked scale that weighs a man by how he looks, so the two sayings stand together and tell the hypocrite from the honest judge.
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) names the judging he forbids, which goes by appearance, and commands the righteous judgment that the Torah asks for.

cards.prose: When Yahusha (Jesus) sends his disciples out, the same line is drawn from the other side. The word goes to whoever will hear it, and where a house or city will not receive it, they *shake off the dust of your feet* and the proclamation stops there. That is the pearl left where it was refused.
cards.member_phrase: whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words
cards.member_sentence: Where the word is not received or heard, Yahusha (Jesus) tells his disciples to leave that place and shake off the dust.

cards.prose: Matthew leaves the good things the Father gives unnamed, and Luke fills them in. The Father who is asked gives the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), so the good gift is the Spirit himself, given to the child who asks.
cards.member_phrase: how much more shall your heavenly Father give the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) to them that ask him
cards.member_sentence: Luke names the good thing the Father gives to those who ask: the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit).

cards.prose: The good things the Father gives reach down to what Yahuah (the LORD) promised the house of Yashar'el (Israel) through Jeremiah, his *law* set in their inward parts and written in their hearts. The asking ends with the commandment no longer standing outside a man but written inside him, and nothing in the gift sets it against the Torah.
cards.member_phrase: I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises to put his law inside his people and write it on their hearts, which is the good gift in full.

cards.prose: Ezekiel spells out the good gift as a heart of flesh in the place of a stony one. The next verse says what that heart is for: *cause you to walk in my statutes, and ye shall keep my judgments, and do them* (Ezekiel 36:27). The Father who answers the child gives what makes his commandments the child's own.
cards.member_phrase: A new heart also will I give you, and a new spirit will I put within you
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) promises a new heart and a new spirit, taking away the stony heart and giving a heart of flesh.

cards.prose: Many go in at the wide gate, and Isaiah had long said what that costs: *yet a remnant of them shall return* (Isaiah 10:22). Those who come through are the ones who stop leaning on the hand that struck them and lean on Yahuah (the LORD) in truth.
cards.member_phrase: the remnant of Yashar'el (Israel), and such as are escaped of the house of Jacob
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah says only a remnant of Yashar'el (Israel) escapes and leans on Yahuah (the LORD) in truth, which is the narrow way's own end.

cards.prose: Matthew sets the many going in at the wide gate against a narrow way, and Zechariah puts a number on the difference: two parts cut off and die, and the third left. The third is not simply spared, since the verse after brings it through the fire to be refined as silver is refined.
cards.member_phrase: two parts therein shall be cut off and die; but the third shall be left therein
cards.member_sentence: Zechariah gives the few a number, two parts cut off and one left, and says the one left is brought through the fire.

cards.prose: The people Yahuah (the LORD) leaves are an afflicted and poor people who trust in his name, and the next verse says what marks them: *shall not do iniquity, nor speak lies* (Zephaniah 3:13). Those who find the narrow way are known by their walk, and by what they will not do.
cards.member_sentence: Zephaniah describes the remnant as a poor and humble people who trust the name of Yahuah (the LORD) and do no iniquity.

cards.prose: A man asks Yahusha (Jesus) the very question the Sermon leaves hanging, whether the saved are few. His answer is a gate, the same strait gate: *Strive to enter in at the strait gate: for many, I say unto you, will seek to enter in, and shall not be able* (Luke 13:24).
cards.member_sentence: Luke records the question whether few are saved, and Yahusha (Jesus) answers by naming the same strait gate.

cards.prose: Yahusha (Jesus) says the wolves come in *sheep’s clothing*. Paul, leaving Ephesus, says the grievous wolves will enter in among the flock and not spare it, and then adds that they will not all come from outside: *Also of your own selves shall men arise, speaking perverse things, to draw away disciples after them* (Acts 20:30).
cards.member_sentence: Paul warns the Ephesian elders that grievous wolves will enter in among the flock and not spare it.

cards.prose: Hearing and doing together is the oldest pairing Yashar'el (Israel) had. When Moses read the book of the covenant in the hearing of the people, they answered that they would do it and be obedient. The wise builder is that answer carried out, and the sayings Yahusha (Jesus) asks to be done are no stranger to the words Moses read.
cards.member_phrase: All that Yahuah (LORD) hath said will we do, and be obedient
cards.member_sentence: The people answer that all Yahuah (the LORD) has said they will do and be obedient, the pattern of hearing and doing.

cards.prose: The rock has a name in the song of Moses: Yahuah (the LORD) is the Rock, his work perfect and all his ways judgment. A house built on his sayings stands on his ways, and the verse after sets beside him a people who corrupted themselves, *a perverse and crooked generation* (Deuteronomy 32:5).
cards.member_sentence: Moses names Yahuah (the LORD) as the Rock whose work is perfect and whose ways are all judgment.

cards.prose: David prays the rock in the middle of a flood, and he says what it holds up under: *the floods of ungodly men made me afraid* (Psalm 18:4). The house that does not fall stands on the one he calls his rock, his fortress and his deliverer, which is Yahuah (the LORD) himself.
cards.member_phrase: Yahuah (LORD) is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer
cards.member_sentence: David calls Yahuah (the LORD) his rock, fortress and deliverer, the ground that holds when the floods come.

cards.prose: James puts the two builders into one line. Hearing alone deceives, and the man who is a doer holds to *the perfect law of liberty* (James 1:25), which is the commandment the Sermon rests on. The rock is the word heard and done, and the sand is hearing without the doing.
cards.member_sentence: James says to be doers of the word and not hearers only, and so restates the wise and foolish builders.
